title: CHAPTER 11: EMPLOYEE WELFARE, HEALTH AND SAFETY

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Employee welfare encompasses efforts to improve the working and living conditions of workers beyond statutory minimums.
Employee health and wellness programs focus on physical, mental, and social well-being while mitigating occupational hazards.
The Employees' Compensation Act, 2010 provides financial security to employees in cases of employment-related injuries or occupational diseases.

blocks.content: Employee welfare refers to the efforts made by employers to improve the living and working conditions of employees beyond the basic wage. It includes both statutory (legally required) and voluntary (employer-initiated) welfare measures.

cells: Canteen, rest rooms, drinking water, first aid, crèche, latrines (Factories Act, Shops Act)
Recreation rooms, gymnasium, employee lounges, bank ATM on premises, cafeteria, library
Housing loans at concessional rates, educational assistance, consumer stores, holiday homes, banks offering staff quarters
PF, gratuity, ESI, workmen's compensation, maternity benefits, bonus
Group insurance, club membership, car loans, consumer loans, additional medical coverage
Education of children, vocational training for family members, cultural programmes, sports, celebrations

rows: Mostly statutory requirements governed by labor laws
Canteens, crèches, drinking water, first-aid facilities
Housing quarters, transport, educational grants, sports clubs

cells: Confidential counselling and support for personal/professional problems; mental health, financial stress, substance abuse
Banking stress-related mental health; 24x7 helpline; counsellor referral; HDFC, ICICI, SBI have EAPs
Banking is high-stress; identify stressors; provide coping tools; organisational and individual interventions
Work overload; target pressure; NPA management stress; shift to relationship banking
Flexible working hours; WFH policies; leave policies; child care support; elder care support
POSH compliance; maternity support; crèche; part-time options for women returnees
Design workstations to prevent musculoskeletal disorders; screen glare; seating; repetitive stress
Branch banking: teller positions; back office IT staff; call centre agents
Periodic health check-ups; monitoring health risks; preventive healthcare
Pre-employment medical; annual health check; wellness camps in banks

items: Note the 2010 amendment that renamed the 'Workmen's Compensation Act' to 'Employees' Compensation Act' to ensure gender neutrality.
Distinguish between intra-mural welfare (statutory provisions inside the factory) and extra-mural welfare (voluntary provisions outside).
Compensation liability under the Act requires an injury arising 'out of and in the course of employment'.

cells: All employees in Schedule II occupations including banking staff; not covered by ESI Act
Employer liable to pay compensation if personal injury by accident arising out of and in course of employment
50% of monthly wages × relevant factor (age-based) or Rs.1,20,000 minimum, whichever is more
60% of monthly wages × relevant factor or Rs.1,40,000 minimum
Percentage of compensation proportional to loss of earning capacity
Injured employee must give employer notice of accident as soon as practicable; failure may reduce compensation
